template_name: Multi-Modal Material Identity Integration via Bayesian Cue Combination
calibration_constraint: Bridge warrant for architectural parameters: FUNCTIONAL (0.50) maximum per pre-panel review

mechanism_chain.process: Occupant perceives architectural material through multiple sensory channels simultaneously: visual texture/color (via ventral visual stream), haptic roughness/temperature/compliance (via somatosensory cortex), acoustic tap/footstep signature (via auditory cortex), olfactory signature (via olfactory bulb → piriform cortex)
mechanism_chain.substrate: Parallel sensory processing in modality-specific cortices

data: Multi-sensory material perception occurs in parallel: visual texture/color, haptic roughness/temperature/compliance, acoustic tap signature, olfactory VOC signature
Modality-specific processing is documented in visual (texture selectivity), somatosensory (material-responsive neurons), auditory (material-dependent resonance), olfactory (VOC-specific receptors)
Integration occurs downstream of modality-specific processing
justification.backing: Ernst & Banks (2002) foundational paper on multisensory material perception. Ernst (2006) review on haptic-visual material integration. Stein & Meredith (1993) on multisensory integration principles.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.6 reflects established neuroanatomy and psychophysical evidence. MECHANISM warrant: parallel processing pathways are anatomically segregated and documented.
justification.rebuttal: Modality-specific processing is not entirely independent; some cross-talk occurs. Top-down expectations can bias early processing.
competing_accounts: Material perception is primarily visual: refuted by blind individual's precise material discrimination
Material perception is amodal: partially true at higher levels but channel-specific processing is foundational
justification.panel_debate_reference: MULTI-I Panel, Feb 2026; Ernst authority on multisensory material integration

mechanism_chain.process: Brain infers whether multi-modal signals share a common cause (same material) using Bayesian causal inference. If common-cause probability is high (seeing and touching the same surface), signals are integrated; if low (hearing a distant sound while touching a nearby surface), they are segregated.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Posterior parietal cortex; superior temporal sulcus — causal inference computation

data: Bayesian causal inference framework: P(common cause | signals) is computed from signal reliability and spatial-temporal alignment
Common-cause probability is high when signals share properties (wood-colored + wood-textured + wood-scented)
Common-cause probability is low when signals conflict (wood-colored laminate + plastic feel + no wood scent)
Integration occurs when P(common cause) > threshold; segregation when P(common cause) < threshold
justification.backing: Körding et al. (2007) explicit Bayesian causal inference model for multisensory integration. Shams & Beierholm (2010) review of Bayesian multisensory models. Neural implementation in posterior parietal cortex and STS (neuroimaging).
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.6 reflects explicit computational models and supporting neuroimaging. MECHANISM warrant: Bayesian causal inference is a documented computational principle in multisensory processing.
justification.rebuttal: Bayesian model is a simplification; actual computations may use heuristics. Prior probability for 'common cause' may vary with context and experience.
competing_accounts: Integration is rule-based (e.g., spatial coincidence only): partially true; spatial-temporal rules are part of the Bayesian computation
Integration is always successful if signals are from same object: refuted by strong incongruence suppressing integration
justification.panel_debate_reference: MULTI-I Panel, Feb 2026; Körding authority on Bayesian multisensory integration

mechanism_chain.process: Integrated material percept is formed by reliability-weighted combination (MLE): each channel contributes in proportion to its signal-to-noise ratio. The combined estimate has lower variance than any individual channel.
mechanism_chain.substrate: Cortical multisensory integration areas; reliability weighting via precision-weighted prediction errors

data: Integrated material percept has lower variance than individual channels
Visual + haptic integration improves discrimination by ~25%
justification.backing: Ernst & Banks (2002) maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) model with human psychophysics. Laboratory measurements of precision gain (30-40% typical). Architectural application discounted to 20-30% (less controlled conditions).
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.55 reflects laboratory evidence but architectural discount for uncontrolled conditions. MECHANISM warrant: MLE principle is established; architectural application is FUNCTIONAL (effectiveness is measured in field).
justification.rebuttal: Laboratory precision gains may not transfer to architecture (shorter contact times, competing visual attention). Individual differences in channel reliability weighting exist.
competing_accounts: Channels are independent and should not be combined: refuted by lower variance in combined estimates
All channels have equal weight: refuted by reliability-weighted evidence from multiple studies
justification.panel_debate_reference: MULTI-I Panel, Feb 2026; Ernst authority on MLE material integration

mechanism_chain.process: Multi-modal material percept generates affective response: material identity (wood, stone, metal, fabric) triggers learned evaluative associations and innate biophilic preferences simultaneously
mechanism_chain.substrate: Orbitofrontal cortex (evaluative), insula (interoceptive affect), amygdala (biophilic salience)

data: Multi-modal material percept (visual + haptic + olfactory) generates affective response
Material identity (wood, stone, metal, fabric) triggers learned evaluative associations (see MATERIAL_CULTURAL_CONDITIONING_001)
Material identity also triggers innate biophilic preferences (see NATURAL_MATERIAL_CONVERGENCE_001)
Affective response is faster and stronger with multi-modal input than visual alone
justification.backing: Ernst (2006) on multisensory affect. Spence (2011) on crossmodal correspondences and affect. Biophilia literature (Kaplan & Kaplan, 1989) on innate material preferences.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.5 reflects convergent evidence but mechanisms are partially inferred. FUNCTIONAL warrant: affective effects are measured behaviorally (ratings, autonomic response).
justification.rebuttal: Affect effects could be mediated by expectation (top-down) rather than multisensory integration per se. Individual preferences vary widely.
competing_accounts: Affect is determined entirely by visual appearance: refuted by blind individual's material preference studies
Multisensory affect is purely additive: partially true but congruence effects suggest non-linear combination
justification.panel_debate_reference: MULTI-I Panel, Feb 2026; Ernst material authority, Spence crossmodal authority

mle_precision_gain_visual_haptic.interpretation: Visual + haptic integration improves material roughness/texture discrimination by ~25% (lab estimate 30–40%, architectural discount to 20–30%, midpoint 25%)

olfactory_precision_addition.interpretation: Adding olfactory channel (natural materials) contributes ~10% additional precision gain. Olfactory is a weaker, less reliable channel with lower MLE weight.

total_multimodal_precision_gain.interpretation: Full multi-modal material experience (see + touch + smell) produces ~35% more precise material percept than visual-only

common_cause_threshold.interpretation: Multi-modal integration requires that signals are spatially co-located (within ~30 cm) and temporally coincident (within ~200 ms). This is satisfied for direct material contact but NOT for visual inspection of distant surfaces.

visual_impairment.effect: Reduced visual reliability → higher weight on haptic and auditory channels → MLE automatically compensates. See MSI_INVERSE_EFFECTIVENESS_002.

age_group.effect: Multisensory integration is generally preserved or enhanced in aging (Laurienti et al., 2006). Older adults may benefit MORE from multi-modal material presentation because single-channel reliability degrades with age.

IC2_AX4_interaction.IC2_body_budget: Body budget state modulates haptic exploration behavior: under allostatic deficit, occupants reduce environmental touch behavior (withdrawal, reduced approach), limiting multi-modal integration opportunities. The precision gain is available only if the occupant ENGAGES with material surfaces.
IC2_AX4_interaction.AX4_perceived_control: Perceived control facilitates exploration: occupants with high environmental control are more likely to touch, explore, and engage multiple sensory channels, maximizing multi-modal integration. Low control restricts exploration to visual-only, forfeiting the precision gain.

cross_template_references: MSI_CONGRUENCY_PRINCIPLE_001 — congruency between channels determines whether integration produces positive or negative affect
MSI_INVERSE_EFFECTIVENESS_002 — degraded unisensory channels increase the multi-modal precision gain
VISUAL-I T1 — visual channel parameters for material texture statistics; no double-counting
name: Multi-Modal Material Identity Integration via Bayesian Cue Combination

touchable_surface_fraction.interpretation: Fraction of material surfaces within arm's reach that can be touched during normal use. Higher fraction → more multi-modal integration opportunities → more precise material percepts.

material_authenticity.interpretation: Authentic materials (real wood, stone, metal) produce congruent multi-modal signals. Simulated materials (wood-print laminate, stone-texture vinyl) produce INCONGRUENT signals — visual says 'wood' but haptic says 'plastic'. Incongruence degrades the precision gain and produces negative affect.

cross_template_interactions.description: Cultural conditioning shapes material identity associations

higher_order_principle: →  pathway: The mechanism by which multi-modal material identity integration via bayesian cue combination operates
